messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT STARTED: Major degradation across hosted inference in us-west-2. Pages sent to on-call. Auto-attach: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/3491234567

alex: On-call. Root symptom: sudden spike in routing-compile queue + an autoscaler race during node recycling, causing a subset of requests to hit fallback model variants with longer cold-starts -> elevated latency and 502s. Currently mitigated by pinning traffic to stable pool.

maria: Thanks — can you summarize customer impact in one paragraph for execs + a short line for statuspage? Need list of affected tenants.

sam: I pulled active sessions list. Affects ~28 customers, 6 high-usage accounts (inc. acme-inc, brightapps). I'll paste PIDs and account IDs to the secure doc.

jordan: For customers: we should lead with what happened, who was affected, what we did immediately, and next steps. Execs want an estimated ETA for full fix and a recommended customer credit.

leah: Legal: avoid admitting systemic negligence. Use "service disruption due to autoscaler race condition that caused elevated errors" and offer a "goodwill credit". No mention of SLA breach unless CS confirms.

alex: Draft timeline (short):
- 12:02 UTC: spike in compile queue and node recycle started
- 12:05 UTC: first 502 alerts from healthchecks
- 12:12 UTC: autoscaler policy hit edge case, churn increased
- 12:25 UTC: mitigation: pinned traffic to stable pool and rolled back recent autoscaler config
- 12:46 UTC: errors dropped to baseline; monitoring set to 2x threshold
- 13:10 UTC: gradual return to normal, follow-up fix planned (autoscaler fix + better canary)

maria: Nice. Can you convert that into a one-paragraph RCA and a 1-sentence status page update? I'll draft the customer email after.

alex: One-paragraph RCA (draft): "Between 12:00–12:45 UTC, a corner case in our autoscaler configuration interacted with a burst of routing-compile work, which caused an increase in node churn and temporarily routed traffic to fallback model pools with higher cold-start latency. This resulted in service errors and elevated latency for a subset of hosted customers. We mitigated the impact by pinning traffic to the stable node pool and rolling back the autoscaler change. A permanent fix (autoscaler race condition patch + improved canarying) is scheduled and will be deployed after validation."

ops-bot: Suggested statuspage blurb (short):
"We experienced a service disruption in us-west-2 between 12:00–12:45 UTC impacting hosted inference. The issue was mitigated; full remediation is in progress. For details and affected accounts, see the customer follow-up."

maria: OK. Draft customer email (customer-facing):
```
Hi <CustomerName>,

We experienced a partial service disruption in us-west-2 on <date> that may have affected your API requests between 12:00–12:45 UTC. Root cause: an autoscaler configuration edge case combined with a burst of compilation work caused temporary routing churn and higher-than-normal error rates. What we did: pinned traffic to stable nodes to restore service, rolled back the autoscaler change, and increased monitoring thresholds. Next steps: a permanent fix (autoscaler race condition patch + stronger canarying) is planned and targeted for deployment this week.

As a gesture of goodwill, we'd like to offer a credit of $X for impacted usage. If you saw production impact, please reply and we will prioritize an account-level review.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

Best,
The Redwood Inference team
```

sam: For the $X credit, propose a sliding credit based on error exposure: 10% for minor blips, 25% for sustained failures >10m, max 50% for severe. We should list affected customers and compute per-account impact before sending.

jordan: Agree with sliding scale. Execs want the total potential credit exposure estimated before we commit. Maria, can you run the cost model?

maria: I'll run numbers. Preliminary ask to finance: rough upper bound if we credit 50% for 6 high-usage accounts for 45 minutes. @finance please ping.

leah: Also recommend we avoid promising exact dollar amounts in public status update — keep that for account-level comms.

alex: Technical action items for postmortem:
- fix: autoscaler race condition patch (PR draft created)
- ops: add canary that simulates routing-compile burst
- infra: increase telemetry on compile queue depth and node churn events
- runbook: add a quick mitigation step to pin traffic to stable pool

maria: Can everyone react with :thumbsup: when they approve the customer email draft and credit approach? I'll hold sending until we have finance numbers and legal OK.

jordan: :thumbsup: from PM side. Approve the messaging.

leah: :thumbsup: legal approves wording and credit plan conditional on finance numbers.

ops-bot: NOTE: Follow-up sync scheduled: Incident retrospective Wednesday 15:00 UTC. Please add details to the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/3491234567

sam: I've exported affected account list to the secure sheet and DM'd finance with the preliminary numbers.

maria: Thanks all — holding send. I'll post a short statuspage update after legal/finance signoff and then coordinate per-account emails. Meeting invite sent for the postmortem.

alex: After-action: we'll prioritize the autoscaler PR and try to have a canary out by EOD tomorrow.

maria: Closing thread for now. If anything changes, I'll reopen. Thanks everyone. :heart:
